question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=4 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The first equation is a false statement. Hence,the system has no solution.

$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-13 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-11\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1} &=-24 \\ {x}_{1} &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=-3$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 4(-3)+{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ {x}_{2} &=1 \\ {x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ (-3)+2(1) &=-2 \\ -1 &=-2\end{aligned}

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=2 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=2 \\ {x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=0$.

Substituting ${x}_{2}=0$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=2 \\ -{x}_{1}+(0) &=2 \\ -{x}_{1} &=2 \\ {x}_{1} &=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=0$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=2 \\ -(-2)+2(0) &=2 \\ 2 &=2\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2}=0$, which means

$$
-2{a}_{1}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-2)+(0)=-2.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 8 \\ -14\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=8 \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-14\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1} & =-6 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & =8 \\ 4(-1)+3{x}_{2} & =8 \\ 3{x}_{2} & =12 \\ {x}_{2} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & =-11 \\ 3(-1)-2(4) & =-11 \\ -11 & =-11,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=4,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+4{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+4=3.
$$
